messages:
emily: @here paging — unusual outbound traffic from staging-log-processor (svc-staging-logs) hitting a small set of external IPs. logs contain partial auth headers in debug payloads. not sure if tokens rotated. tagging sec-eng and oncall.

oncall-pd-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-8942 created and paged to raj. Escalation policy: infra-oncall -> sec-eng.

raj: acknowledged. joining. quick ask: is this app in dedicated VPC or a shared infra?

emily: staging runs in customer-shared subnet (staging-vpc), but svc-staging-logs has restricted S3 write role. the debug logger was toggled on last night via deploy.

maria: copied logs to /tmp and grep'd for "Authorization:" — found ~12 occurrences in the last 2 hours with Bearer tokens (truncated). external IPs: 45.76.33.12, 3.210.44.5.

leo: those IPs resolve to a small hosting provider, likely a scraper. checked outbound NAT gateway flow logs: ~3k connections between 01:05-01:18 UTC.

sec-eng-bot: Incident level: HIGH. Recommended immediate actions: 1) block outbound to listed IPs at NAT; 2) disable debug logging on svc-staging-logs; 3) rotate service principal keys for svc-staging-logs; 4) start customer-impact sweep.

raj: doing steps in parallel. Maria — can you push an env toggle to turn off debug? I'll patch the NAT ACL and rotate keys after.

maria: pushing a hotfix now. command: ```kubectl set env deploy/staging-log-processor DEBUG=false -n staging```

maria: hotfix applied, logs show DEBUG=false. verifying no new Authorization headers in recent log tail.

raj: blocking at NAT now: ```aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0123abcd --rule-number 100 --egress --cidr 45.76.33.12/32 --protocol -1 --rule-action deny``` and same for 3.210.44.5. applied.

leo: seeing drop counters incrementing on NAT. good.

raj: rotating svc account keys. steps: creating new role key, updating secret in secrets-manager, redeploying. ```aws iam create-access-key --user-name svc-staging-logs``` (we'll delete old key after verification).

emily: notify customers? this is staging-only; no production namespaces affected. but double-check if any tokens in CI or shared artifact storage.

maria: grep across artifact storage (s3://redwood-artifacts/staging-*) — found two archived debug bundles with truncated tokens in object logs. downloading for audit and then rotating keys used to sign those artifacts.

sec-eng-bot: ACTIONS logged: NAT block applied; debug disabled; new access key created; old key marked for deletion after 30m verification window. Start a 1:1 customer impact check for any customers using staging images in prerelease.

raj: after rotate, redeploy done. verifying services healthy. health checks green. Will delete old key in 30m unless rollback required.

maria: audit notes: tokens in debug dumps are already expired (timestamps truncated), but we cannot be certain downstream copies didn't persist. we'll run a grep across internal ops channels and artifact indices.

leo: opening firewall request to block / monitor entire CIDR range for that provider. submitting ticket to netops.

emily: handing off to night oncall — raj, please coordinate with sec team for follow-up remediation, runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/sec/token-exposure. if anything changes page the incident channel and PD. I'm going offline in ~10m but reachable by DM.

raj: noted. I'll keep the incident open and run a quick customer-impact scan. participants: @maria will continue artifact audit, @leo will monitor NAT counters, sec-eng will look for lateral movement.

sec-eng-bot: Handoff checklist: "1) Confirm old keys deleted; 2) Confirm no other services used same credential; 3) Ensure artifact retention/access logs captured; 4) Trigger alert for any use of deleted key."

maria: continuing grep, logging findings to the incident ticket. so far no sign of replacement keys used externally.

raj: last status before leaving shift: NAT blocks in place, debug off, new keys active, old key scheduled deletion in 28m, no production impact detected. leaving follow-ups to night: run full S3 audit, rotate any matching keys, and check CI tokens.

emily: thanks team. will update customers if we find any confirmed external use. :thumbsup:
